venue.name: Campbell River Art Gallery
venue.description: The Campbell River Art Gallery is a non-profit public art gallery on Shoppers Row in downtown Campbell River. It opened in 1994 and is the city's only public gallery, showing contemporary art by professional artists in a Main Gallery and a Satellite Gallery, with a separate studio space used for art activities. Staff run guided tours of the current exhibition followed by an art activity for school and community groups, and an art educator will also come into a classroom to teach a technique. Both are charged as one fee for the whole group.
venue.address: 1235 Shoppers Row, Campbell River, BC V9W 2C7

facility_notes.washrooms: There is one gender inclusive washroom located by the West entrance (near Shoppers Row)
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Wheelchair accessible, accessed by two main doors to the Centennial Building, with an accessible parking space at the rear of the building

venue.hours_notes: Gallery and gallery shop 10am to 4pm. Tuesday to Sunday in summer, Tuesday to Saturday from Sept. 7. Office hours Tuesday to Friday 10am to 4pm, closed for stat holidays.

programs.name: School & Community Group Tours
programs.description: A staff led guided tour of the current or an upcoming exhibition, followed by an art activity. The gallery describes it as a 30 minute tour with a 1 hour art activity, running an hour and a half in all, for K to 12 and beyond. The fee is $110 for the group, or $100 for School District 72 groups. Booking goes to the programs manager by email.
programs.what_children_do: Go round the gallery with a member of staff who talks about the exhibition that is up, then spend about an hour on an art activity linked to what they have just looked at.
programs.our_note: An hour and a half with a sit down making session in the middle suits a group that can manage a quiet gallery for the first half. They publish no limit on group size and nothing about how many adults to bring, so settle both in the email when you book.
programs.practical_summary: There are washrooms on site and the building is wheelchair accessible, with an accessible parking space at the back. Nowhere to eat lunch and nowhere for a bus to wait are mentioned, so those are worth a call.
programs.evidence: 30 minute Tour with 1 hour art activity: $110.00 per group ($100 for School District 72) K to 12 and beyond.

programs.name: Gallery in the School Program
programs.description: An art educator from the gallery comes to the classroom to teach one technique or genre, with acrylic painting, self portraiture, animals in art, portfolio prep and colour theory given as examples, tied to the gallery's exhibitions and permanent collection. The fee is $110 using the school's own materials, or $100 for School District 72. The gallery describes it as one hour per class and says it can fit around the school timetable.
programs.what_children_do: Stay in their own classroom and make something alongside a visiting art educator, working on a single technique such as acrylic painting or colour theory for the hour.
programs.our_note: This is the version for when getting a group out of the building is the hard part. The fee is written as covering the visit with your own materials, so ask exactly what they want you to have ready on the table before the day.
programs.practical_summary: This one happens in your own room, so the gallery's washrooms, parking and access do not come into it. What materials you are expected to supply is not spelled out, so ask when you email.
programs.extra_fees_note: $100 for School District 72. The $110 is stated as being with use of school materials.
programs.evidence: Fees: $110 with use of school materials ($100 for School District 72)

gaps: Whether they take a group of children under school age is not stated. Both programmes are written for K to 12, and the tour adds 'and beyond', which reads as older rather than younger.
No maximum or minimum group size is published for either programme.
How many adults have to come with a group is not published.
How much notice they need for a booking is not published.
Nowhere to eat lunch is mentioned anywhere on the site, indoors or out, and there is no mention of where a bus can stop or park.
Whether GST is added to the $110 is not stated on the education page.
Which days and months the group tours run is not published, and no start times are given.
General admission prices for a walk in visit are not published, so we do not know whether the gallery is free to enter.

INFERENCE FLAG. The classroom visit is priced only as 'Fees: $110 with use of school materials ($100 for School District 72)'. It does not say per class, per group or per child. We have recorded it as a whole group fee because the tour immediately above it on the same page is written as '$110.00 per group' and the classroom line says 'One hour per class'. That is our reading, not their words, and it is the single thing most worth confirming by email.
The prices carry no year or season on the page, so there is no way to tell from the page how old they are.
The site says it offers digital tours as well as in person ones, but gives no length, age range or price for them, so no digital programme has been recorded.

The Art Hive is a weekly open studio for adults from the unhoused and lived experience community, not a children's programme, so it has not been recorded as one. The Digital Programs page is an archive of past talks and workshops rather than anything bookable.
The Open Graph image on the education page is the School Tours banner rather than a photograph of arriving at the building, so the hero is the exterior photograph from their What We Do page instead.
Alt text for the three generated entries was written after opening each image URL in a browser and looking at the picture, not from the file name.

values: Tuesday to Sunday in summer, Tuesday to Saturday from Sept. 7
conflicts.note: Their home page says the gallery is open Tuesday to Sunday. Their hours page says that is the summer pattern and that Sundays stop from September 7. We use the hours page. Worth confirming before you plan anything on a Sunday.
Their page describes the classroom visit as K to 12 in one line and all ages two lines later. If your group is younger than kindergarten, ask which they mean when you book.
